ledger.claim: The gps_trace governs the POL-RD-01 threshold test, and it is unimpaired: 229 fixes at the 10-second expected interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) is met. The trace places the vehicle at 27.18 km travelled, not the 27.2 km rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing measurement.

Against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km the trace shows an excess of 6.18 km, which is 29.4% of the optimal route. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass: the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms AND exceeds 20% in proportional terms, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00101 and the 10:21:05 pickup timestamp match across the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and a threshold-meeting excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause, and he points to none.

The driver's own in-app message — 'sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now' — is a driver admission recorded in the chat_log, one of the independent corroborating sources POL-RD-07(ii) names, and it squarely corroborates the deviation. His counterparty_statement repeats the admission ('I took a wrong turn at the MCE exit'), and no exculpatory account appears anywhere in the record.

No exculpatory clause rescues the driver. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and the absence cannot carry the driver's excuse under POL-RD-13; the chat_log shows no rider instruction to detour as POL-RD-04(a) requires, and no rider message names any waypoint; no pickup or dropoff amendment exists for POL-RD-05 (both amendment timestamps are null); the fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 is out; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The deviation stands at the measured figure.

Under POL-RD-02 the refund is arithmetic: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63, with no ERP, toll, surcharge, waiting fee or promo line to adjust. The refund is charged_total 35.64 minus 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, giving SGD 8.05.

The refund of 8.05 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is not a NO_ACTION; and at 22.5% of charged_total it is well below the 90% full-refund share, so it is not a FULL_REFUND. The correct outcome for this rider-filed dispute is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05, returning to the rider the distance and time charged for a detour he never asked for.

There is no pass-through line to correct or double-count: erp_lines is empty and the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00, and no airport surcharge arises on a trip that neither originates nor terminates at an airport. The POL-RD-02 figure therefore neither reduces nor supplements on POL-RD-09 grounds, and the rider's remedy is the 8.05 refund alone.

The refund the rider can recover is fixed by POL-RD-02 arithmetic, not by the SGD 10.00 he contests. On the booked optimal route the recomputed fare is SGD 27.63 (base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min, the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee) and charged_total is SGD 35.64, so the refund is SGD 8.01 rounded up to SGD 8.05. No clause in this policy widens that figure.

On the trace that governs under POL-RD-01 the excess is 6.18 km, being 29.43% of the 21.0 km optimal route. That clears the establishment gate (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) but is short of BOTH material thresholds - 8.0 km absolute and 50% - so this can only ever be a POL-RD-02 partial-refund case, and the POL-RD-06 uplift to FULL_REFUND of charged_total is not available on this record.

Even if the driver profile were consulted under POL-RD-06, no repeat-deviation pattern is established against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3-flag limb, and 0 divided by 812 completed_trips_90d is 0, below the 0.05 ratio limb (with the required minimum of 40 trips), so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) can fire. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and may not be substituted for it.

ledger.claim: There is no billing-integrity or pass-through correction to add to the rider's refund: the distance charged (27.2 km) matches the governing trace distance (27.18 km), and tolls/ERP, the optimal-route ERP and the airport surcharge are all 0.00, so POL-RD-09(4) identifies no phantom line. Any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and could never be added on top of it.

Even at its highest the rider's case yields PARTIAL_REFUND, not FULL_REFUND: the SGD 8.05 refund is about 22.5% of the SGD 35.64 charged, far below the 90% share that POL-RD-02 requires before a full refund issues, so the driver's monetary exposure on this trip is bounded at the partial figure and nothing more.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I have checked the trip record (EV-TRIP-00101), GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101), fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00101), chat log (EV-CHAT-00101), profiles and the missing advisory (EV-ADVIS-00101-01). The GPS trace is complete and unimpaired: 229 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. It shows 27.18 km travelled against the booked optimal route of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km (29.4%). That passes POL-RD-01: the excess is over 0.8 km and over 20%, so a route deviation is established. It does not pass either material threshold (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so POL-RD-06 is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral arises. The driver’s chat admission that he missed the exit is consistent, but the unimpaired trace alone carries the finding. No exculpatory clause applies: the traffic advisory is missing (EV-ADVIS-00101-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and cannot excuse the deviation; there is no rider-requested detour or waypoint; there is no pickup/dropoff amendment; the fare is METERED; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not pooled. Under POL-RD-02, recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 21.0 + 0.28 × 26.0) × 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. charged_total = 35.64. refund = 35.64 − 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to 8.05. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.05. No POL-RD-09 pass-through correction applies (ERP/tolls/surcharges are all zero). No driver compensation is due: the fare did not bill less distance than the trace. The driver’s arguments that the refund is fixed at 8.05 and that no full refund is available are accepted; the rider’s arguments that the deviation is established and the refund is 8.05 are accepted. The driver-profile reference to prior_deviation_flags is context only and was not used; no repeat-deviation pattern is established. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect of 8.05 exceeds the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling is issued but the amount is held for the POL-GEN-05 human release queue rather than executed automatically; that queue step is not an escalation and does not change the ruling. Confidence 0.98, capped at 1.0 by the weight-1.0 artifacts carrying the deciding facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
